# moneyer

LNURLcash (LUD-25) mint for Node 24+. Strikes Lightning bearer notes:
paying an invoice it issues mints a note whose spend secret is the
invoice's payment preimage, or a secret the buyer named with `h` on the
pay callback. ESM-only. MIT.

Install: not yet on npm - build from source (see README)
Run: node dist/cli.js --dev   (fake funding source, prints a funded note)

Draft spec: https://github.com/lnurl/luds/pull/301
Conformance: https://github.com/TheCryptoDonkey/lnurlcash-conformance
Companion wallet: @forgesworn/notecase
Client library to build against a mint: lnurlcash-kit

## Rules this SERVICE follows (and any mint MUST)

1. A mint quote MUST be named. The payer sends `comment=hex(sha256(secret))`
   on the pay callback (LUD-12, and the payRequest advertises
   `commentAllowed: 64`); a missing or malformed comment is refused before
   any invoice is issued. The note is credited at that hash, so the secret
   is the payer's alone. The payment preimage is settlement proof and never
   a bearer credential - it is known to the funding source, to every node on
   the route, and to anyone who polls verify with the payment hash written
   inside the invoice. `h` is an additive alias for the same commitment and
   never replaces the comment. Because the note is not keyed by the
   preimage, a funding source whose node chooses its own preimages
   (phoenixd, NIP-47 make_invoice) can back a mint. LUD-25 Part 2: the
   comment may instead be `cp1<pk>`, and the note is keyed by that key.
2. Mutations are atomic: all named k1 burn and all outputs mint, or
   nothing happens. A note named twice in one request is refused, compared
   by the note each k1 spends: one Part 2 note has many valid ck1 strings.
3. p1/p2 (older names h/h2, still accepted; both spellings of one output
   must agree) are WALLET-supplied hashes or cp1 keys; the mint never generates a
   replacement secret, and refuses output ids that already exist as
   notes, as mint-invoice payment hashes, or as a note another payer has
   already bought with `h`. A malformed `h` on the pay callback is
   refused BEFORE an invoice is issued; a colliding one gets the same
   oracle-free refusal a colliding mutation output gets. The reply
   carries mintToHash: true when the invoice was bound, and the
   payRequest and mint address advertise mintToHash: true.
4. Melt OK means IN FLIGHT. The note burns only on confirmed payment,
   restores only on confirmed non-payment, and stays pending otherwise.
   A clean failure REPORT is not confirmation (hodl invoices).
5. A melt invoice must equal the note total exactly, or state no amount
   at all, in which case the mint sends the whole-sat floor of the note's
   value and refuses with 'insufficient value' when that is zero. It must
   not be one this mint issued, and must not repeat an earlier melt's
   payment hash.
   On a SHARED funding source the node's own payment history is the only
   dedupe that spans every consumer: pre-check it before reserving the
   note, and treat the node's "payment already exists" refusal as a
   distinct restorable outcome - never confirm a melt against a payment
   this mint did not initiate.
6. Fee algebra (LUD-25, when a fee is advertised): base_fee_msat comes
   out of every split's CHANGE, never the requested amount; a merge of n
   notes refunds (n-1) base fees; a change that cannot cover the fee or
   would land at zero refuses with 'insufficient value'. The proportional
   part applies at mint time only.
7. Reason strings are protocol surface: 'pending',
   'Invalid or already spent k1.', 'Unknown note.', 'Note already spent.',
   'missing p1', 'missing p2' (withdraw callback), 'missing h' (pay
   callback), 'insufficient value' - wallets classify on them.
8. minSendable must survive the mint's own fee (grossUpForMintFee of the
   dust floor), or the mint advertises an amount it will refuse.

## Library API

createMoneyer(config, deps?) -> {url, port, store, backend, signer, reconcile, close}
verifyAnnouncement(content, mintPubkey) -> {valid, document}
  kind 30078 / d=lnurlcash-mint: a mint announcing itself, content = its
  discovery document + sig by the note signing key. MONEYER_ANNOUNCE=true,
  off by default.
configFromEnv(env?) -> MoneyerConfig     MONEYER_* environment variables
  MONEYER_ONION_URL: this mint as a Tor hidden service. A request arriving on
  that Host gets every URL (callback, withdrawLink, payLink, the address in
  the metadata) built from it; anything else falls through to
  MONEYER_PUBLIC_ORIGIN. The Host header only CHOOSES between origins the
  operator configured - it never builds one.
createFakeBackend() -> LightningBackend with .control test hooks
createClnBackend({url, rune}) / createLndBackend({url, macaroon})
createNoteSigner(privHex) -> {pubkey, sign(noteId, amountMsat)}
fakeBolt11({amountMsat, paymentHashHex, memo?}) -> decodable, unpayable invoice
NoteStore - SQLite store; notes by sha256(k1), never secrets

## Endpoints

/.well-known/lnurlp/{user}  LUD-16 payRequest (mints)
/.well-known/lnurlw/{user}  LUD-25 mint address (experimental)
/p/cb                       LUD-06 pay callback (comment names the note: hash or cp1)
/verify/{payment_hash}      LUD-21 verify (mint invoices AND melt payments)
/w                          LUD-03 informational GET by k1 (secret or ck1) or p (hash or cp1, older h); a cp1 note carries its cs1 as sig
/w/cb                       melt / rotate / split / merge; inputs secrets or ck1, outputs p1/p2 hashes or cp1 (or older h/h2); cp1 outputs certified as cs1
POST /names                 claim a name (NIP-98; the signer owns it); body {name, note?, cx1?}.
                            The owner may resend {name, cx1} to set a branch, or cx1: null to clear it
/z/cb/{name}                zap invoice for a name. With a cx1 the settled note is credited to the
                            holder's next key, and the kind 2525 gift wrap carries no secret:
                            /w?p=<cp1>&amount=&sig=<cs1>&i=<index> plus an `i` tag. The index is
                            taken at settlement, never at the invoice, and occupied keys are skipped
